figure1.title: PNS volume has risen 16-fold since its 2018 trough
figure1.subtitle: But it is only 55% above its 2015 level: 64555 billing collapsed between 2016 and 2018 before growing every year since. Epidural injections declined over the same period.
figure1.footnote: Source: CMS Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners - by Provider and Service + CMS Medicare Geographic Variation (National/State/County), data years 2017-2024. Accessed 2026-08-25. Analysis: 100% free public data, no license required.  CPT 62323 was created in 2017, so all series are indexed to 2017.

figure2.title: The top 10% of providers deliver 100% of all PNS volume
figure2.subtitle: Gini 0.98 for PNS versus 0.68 for epidurals across the same 11,286 providers. Only 268 providers billed PNS at all, versus 7,346 for epidurals.
figure2.footnote:
Source: CMS Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners - by Provider and Service, data years 2024. Accessed 2026-08-25. Analysis: 100% free public data, no license required.  Ranked over the common universe of 11,286 providers billing any study code in 2024; Gini CIs are 2,000-resample percentile bootstraps.
IMPORTANT: CMS suppresses any provider-code row with 10 or fewer beneficiaries, so low-volume providers are invisible. That truncation biases measured concentration DOWNWARD - these estimates are conservative.

figure3.title: 14 states still had no Medicare provider billing PNS in 2024
figure3.subtitle: Deserts are shrinking fast - but 24% of fee-for-service beneficiaries (6,722,156 people) still live in a state with fewer than 3 PNS providers.
figure3.footnote: Source: CMS Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners - by Provider and Service + CMS Medicare Geographic Variation (National/State/County), data years 2015-2024. Accessed 2026-08-25. Analysis: 100% free public data, no license required.  A state counts as zero when no provider clears the 11-beneficiary reporting floor, which is itself an access signal.

figure4.title: General pain-physician supply predicts PNS volume - but only weakly, and it survives adjustment
figure4.subtitle: Model A: general density IRR 1.108. Model B adds neuromodulation-capable density: general density barely moves (1.089) and stays significant. This does NOT support the hypothesis that general supply is the wrong denominator.
figure4.footnote: Source: CMS Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners - by Provider and Service + CMS Medicare Geographic Variation (National/State/County), data years 2015-2024. Accessed 2026-08-25. Analysis: 100% free public data, no license required.  Negative binomial, log FFS-beneficiary offset, year fixed effects, SE clustered on state. N = 510 state-years, 51 clusters. Pseudo R2: A = 0.018, B = 0.022. Overdispersion alpha = 6.55 (Poisson would require alpha = 0).

figure5.title: State income shows no detectable relationship with PNS access
figure5.subtitle: Pearson r = 0.013 (p = 0.93); Spearman rho = 0.073 (p = 0.61); n = 51 states. The expected income gradient is NOT present in these data.
figure5.footnote: Source: CMS Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners - by Provider and Service, data years 2024. Accessed 2026-08-25. Analysis: 100% free public data, no license required.  Income: US Census Small Area Income and Poverty Estimates, 2024. SAIPE replaces the ACS API, which now requires a key for every request.

figure5b.title: Dual-eligible share shows no detectable linear relationship with PNS access
figure5b.subtitle: Pearson r = -0.135 (p = 0.34); Spearman rho = -0.252 (p = 0.07); n = 51 states. The rank correlation leans negative but does not reach significance.
figure5b.footnote: Source: CMS Medicare Physician & Other Practitioners - by Provider and Service + CMS Medicare Geographic Variation (National/State/County), data years 2024. Accessed 2026-08-25. Analysis: 100% free public data, no license required.  Dual-eligible share is BENE_DUAL_PCT from the CMS Geographic Variation file.

figure6.title: Spinal cord stimulation access research outnumbers PNS access research 4 to 1
figure6.subtitle: Across 2015-2024: 168 SCS papers versus 44 PNS papers on matched access/utilization queries.
figure6.footnote:
Source: NCBI PubMed E-utilities esearch, accessed 2026-08-25. Exact queries (identical except the therapy term):
SCS: ("spinal cord stimulation"[Title/Abstract]) AND (access[Title/Abstract] OR utilization[Title/Abstract] OR disparities[Title/Abstract] OR "geographic variation"[Title/Abstract] OR epidemiology[Title/Abstract])
PNS: ("peripheral nerve stimulation"[Title/Abstract]) AND (access[Title/Abstract] OR utilization[Title/Abstract] OR disparities[Title/Abstract] OR "geographic variation"[Title/Abstract] OR epidemiology[Title/Abstract])
Caveat: publication counts from a keyword query proxy research attention; they are not proof of absence.
